decisions.question: Approve corrected accounts before valuation
decisions.answer: Approve the corrected accounts as the student-certified primary case, with the €9,000 inventory conflict, inferred €45,000 opening supplier payable and zero-evidence insurance schedule disclosed.
decisions.aiProposal: Use corrected accounts for board review with explicit €9,000 inventory and €45,000 opening-AP qualifications; student approval remains pending
decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 recommends board review only, with unresolved inventory and inferred opening payable clearly disclosed.
decisions.studentReasoning: I approved the corrected accounts because the primary statements use the strongest available evidence and separately disclose rather than hide the unresolved €9,000 inventory conflict, inferred €45,000 opening AP and zero-evidence insurance treatment. The balance sheet reconciles as €406,000 liabilities plus €134,000 equity equals €540,000 assets. I did not accept management’s €312,000 profit because it omits evidence-supported accounting corrections. The reconstructed €74,000 profit reconciles through the recognised costs and €12,000 interest; if €405,000 inventory consumption is later confirmed, profit would decrease to €65,000.

decisions.question: Use claimed management profit for earn-out
decisions.answer: Reject management’s €312,000 earn-out basis; use the student-certified €74,000 primary profit, subject to the disclosed €9,000 inventory sensitivity.

decisions.independentChallenge: Agent 2 rejects management earn-out and recommends €74,000 primary profit, subject to inventory uncertainty.
decisions.studentReasoning: I rejected management’s €312,000 profit because it was not supported by the complete evidence. After incorporating the evidence-supported adjustments, including inventory costs, payroll, depreciation, the R-17 bad debt and the legal provision, the reconstructed profit is €74,000. Owner distributions of €110,000 are not expenses and do not reduce profit. If the alternative €405,000 inventory consumption were confirmed, COGS would increase by €9,000 and profit would fall from €74,000 to €65,000.
